text:
carla: Quick heads-up — onboarding hf/distil-chat-lite into RW. Tool calls in our test harness are being swallowed when chat templates include the `<<JSON_MODE>>` sentinel. Repro below.

 dmitri: repro pls

 carla: Root prompt we send (simplified):

 ```
 <system>
 You are an assistant. Use JSON_MODE for tool outputs.
 </system>
 <user>
 Get user profile and run custom_tool({"id":123})
 </user>
 ```

 When the model emits the tool tag it often becomes token-split across the `role` anchor, so the RW tokenizer/bridge treats the tool tag like normal text and our tool-detection regex misses it. Example output we capture: 

 ```
 assistant: {
   "role": "assistant",
   "content": "<tool_start>custom_tool</tool_start>â{\"id\":123}â
"
 }
 ```

 priya: ugh, looks like UTF-8 curly quotes after quantization? those â sequences are suspicious. Which tokenizer / vocab did you use?

 carla: Using HF tokenizer from model card: `distil-chat-lite-tokenizer` with the default special tokens. On our side we run post-quantize tests (int8) and the quant pipeline sometimes emits non-ascii markers while merging special tokens.

 anya: can you dump the raw token ids around the tag?

 carla: pasted below (ids trimmed):

 ```
 tokens: [1012, 502, 3001, 9999, 40000, 2, 40001, 12, 345, 9999]
 repr: ["<", "tool_start", "custom_tool", "<", "JSON_MODE", ">", "{", "\"id\":", "123", "}"]
 ```

 quant-lab: FYI we saw a similar artifact when using the `grouped_quant` pass. It merges byte sequences and can collapse token boundaries around rare special tokens.

 dmitri: hypothesis: HF tokenizer's special token for JSON_MODE is a multi-byte sentinel that our RW tokenizer mapping doesn't normalize, so the model output includes a partially escaped sequence. Our tool-tag regex expects contiguous `<tool_start>NAME</tool_start>` with no intervening bytes.

 priya: quick mitigation: importer should run a normalization pass: 1) map HF special token ids to RW canonical sentinels, 2) re-run detokenization with exact vocab, 3) perform regex-based merge for split tags. I'll open a small PR for the importer.

 carla: for testing i hacked a local patch that post-processes text with this heuristic: replace /(</?tool_start>)([^<]{0,20})(</tool_start>)/ with collapse when intervening bytes include non-printables. It recovers ~85% of cases. Not perfect.

 dmitri: can we add a failing unit test? sample input + quantized model output that splits the tag. Add to `ml/bridge/tests/test_tool_tag_reassembly.py`.

 priy a: on it — will include an explicit `config.json` mapping note. Proposed change to importer config example:

 ```json
 {
   "special_tokens": {
     "json_mode": "<<JSON_MODE>>",
     "tool_start": "<tool_start>",
     "tool_end": "<\/tool_start>"
   },
   "tokenizer_source": "hf", 
   "normalize_after_quant": true
 }
 ```

 eng-bot: job 884: model-importer pipeline finished (https://ci.redwood.local/884) :white_check_mark:

 anya: also let's run the eval suite with the canary that tests toolcall parsing and function-calling metrics — group `toolcall-parser` on `evals/benchmarks`. We need to ensure PR doesn't hide real regressions.

 carla: agree. Also note: model emits correct structure in non-quantized runs, so this is a quantization + tokenizer edge. Recording as onboarding note for this model: "distil-chat-lite: special-token boundary fragility under grouped_quant".

 priya: plan: small importer patch + unit test + a quant-job that re-runs on 3 seeds. If flaky, escalate to quant team. I'll attach the PR number when ready.

 dmitri: thanks. if we still see >5% tool-detection failures at eval time, fallback to non-grouped quant for this model on Dedicated slots. :thumbsup:

 carla: thanks all. filing a short internal doc with repro and mitigations. Link when uploaded.
